pinterest.title: Classical Wedding Processional Songs for Quartet, Organ or Piano
pinterest.description: Classical processional pieces are easy to arrange for quartet, organ, harp or piano, and simple to time to the walk. Pachelbel's Canon in D can be stretched or shortened around your arrival, Handel's The Arrival of the Queen of Sheba keeps a wedding party moving, and Wagner's Bridal Chorus signals the couple from the first bar. Read the full guide.

Live music follows the room. Recorded music needs a reliable sound system, someone to press play and a back-up copy.

instagram_carousel.caption:
The walk down the aisle is the shortest part of the ceremony and the one everyone remembers. The music sets its pace and mood.

Our new guide, 40 Wedding Processional Songs to Walk Down the Aisle To, groups the songs by style rather than ranking them: classical, church and hymns, instrumental and modern.

How to choose:
- Start with the setting, then think about pace. A slow piece suits a long aisle; a brisker one keeps a large wedding party moving.
- Use one piece for the wedding party and a clearly different one for the couple, so guests know when to stand.
- Time it at the rehearsal. Live players can repeat a section; with a recording, fade at a natural phrase.

A few from the list:
- Classical: Canon in D, Johann Pachelbel. Bridal Chorus, Richard Wagner.
- Church: Ave Maria, Franz Schubert. Trumpet Tune, Henry Purcell.
- Instrumental: Nuvole Bianche, Ludovico Einaudi. River Flows in You, Yiruma.
- Modern: Perfect, Ed Sheeran. At Last, Etta James.

Marrying abroad? Ask the venue and musicians early what a quote covers, who runs the sound and what the back-up is, and get the terms in writing.

Planning the music for a ceremony overseas? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Full guide at the link in bio.
